beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At 3,363 metres, it sends a text: it has dropped two weights. The ship answers. Nothing comes back.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: 7 seconds after that message, the hull gave way. What broke it was there long before that morning.

beats.say: Not one mistake, but a chain of them: a hull nobody certified, a bang on dive 80, and warnings that were waved away.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: This story has seven parts: the trip, the pressure, the hull, the warnings, the last dive, the findings, and what changed.

params.place: the North Atlantic at the dive site, morning

moments.what: the chapter card types on: the trip
Titan rides its launch platform in the swell
a label pins to the sub

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What was Titan? A small submersible built by a company called OceanGate, to carry paying guests to the Titanic.

moments.what: the wreck pin drops on the chart
the ocean fills in blue

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The wreck lies in the North Atlantic, about 370 nautical miles southeast of St. John's, Newfoundland.

moments.what: a cut through the ocean draws on
the depth axis grows down to the wreck
the wreck sits on the seabed line
the water darkens toward the bottom
a small sub outline appears at the surface

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It rests 3,880 metres down, on the ocean floor, in total darkness. How do you get people there and back?

params.place: the launch platform in the swell

moments.what: the camera glides along Titan on the platform
a price tag swings from the sub's rail
the tag settles, the window glows
the platform dips in the swell
a dive clock tag types on

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: OceanGate typically charged $250,000 for a seat. A dive to the wreck was meant to last about eight hours.

params.place: the launch platform at dawn

moments.what: dawn light rises over the platform
five small figures cross the platform to the open dome
the first figure steps in
the second follows
the last three climb in

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On the morning of the dive, five people climbed in: the pilot, who ran the company, a Titanic expert, and three paying guests.

params.place: the front dome of Titan, on the platform

moments.what: the dome swings down onto the ring
bolts spin in one by one
a bolt count tag ticks up
a diver's lamp passes the dome

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then the crew bolted the front dome shut, with 18 bolts. Only the crew outside could open it again.

params.place: under the surface, below the launch platform

moments.what: the platform floods and slips under
the sub lifts off the platform
Titan drops away into the blue
a descent-rate tag types on
bubbles stream up past the camera

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At about 9 in the morning, Titan let go of its platform and began to sink. How fast? About 30 metres every minute.

params.place: a cross-section of the ocean above the wreck

moments.what: the sub outline starts down the ocean cut
a clock in the margin turns
arrows press in on the sub outline
the arrows grow and turn red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The trip down was meant to take about two and a half hours. And the whole way, something was squeezing the hull harder and harder.

params.place: the surface line of the ocean cut

moments.what: the chapter card types on: the pressure
a one-inch square draws on the surface line
a small weight lands on the square
the gauge reads the sea-level figure

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What is squeezing it? At sea level, the air presses on every square inch with about 14.7 pounds.

params.place: the seabed end of the ocean cut

moments.what: the square slides down to the seabed
the water column darkens above it
a stack of weights crushes onto the square
the square outline flashes red
the weight stack shudders
the gauge needle swings to the deep figure, red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At the Titanic, the water presses with 5,554.5 pounds on every square inch.

params.place: beside Titan in the dark water

moments.what: the camera pushes in on the hull
a car-sized load symbol ghosts onto the hull
a small square outlines on the carbon
the square repeats across the hull

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That is more than the weight of a family car, on every square inch of the hull.

params.place: a cutaway drawing of Titan's pressure hull

moments.what: the hull cutaway draws on
the wall thickens in outline
five small seated figures appear inside
the inside fills pale blue: normal air
arrows press on the wall from every side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: How does anything survive that? A pressure hull keeps the people inside at normal air pressure, and takes the whole load itself.

params.place: Titan with its fairing cut away, in a studio of dark water

moments.what: the white fairing fades away
the black carbon cylinder lights its outline
a thickness tag pins to the wall
the two rings glint
the domes slide out and back in

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Titan's hull was a tube of carbon fibre, 5 inches thick, capped at each end with a titanium dome.

params.place: Titan with its fairing cut away, in a studio of dark water

moments.what: the camera slides along the black cylinder
a glue line glows where tube meets ring
the ring glints
the dome slides out and bolts back on
a label pins to the joint

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The carbon tube was glued into two titanium rings, and the domes were bolted onto the rings.

params.place: a materials bench on the drafting sheet

moments.what: a carbon tube and a steel tube sit on scales
the carbon side rises: lighter
arrows press in on the carbon tube
arrows pull it apart, a question mark

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why carbon fibre? It is light. The company's chief believed it was better at being squeezed than stretched.

params.place: beside Titan in the dark water

moments.what: the hull glows amber
it fades back to black
the cycle repeats faster
a red tag stamps: never tested

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But what happens to that tube when it is squeezed and released, dive after dive? OceanGate never properly tested it.

params.place: a pressure test tank in a laboratory

moments.what: the chapter card types on: the hull
a small hull drawing lowers into a test tank
the tank's depth gauge climbs
the model crumples, red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Were there early warnings? In 2016, a one-third scale model of the hull imploded in a test, at about 4,200 metres.

params.place: test-dive waters in the Bahamas

moments.what: Titan hangs in blue test water
a year tag pins to the hull
the sub sinks slowly past the camera
the window glows with figures inside
sound rings pulse off the hull

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The first full-size hull was built in 2018. On deep test dives, people inside heard cracking sounds.

params.place: a magnified cut through the hull wall

moments.what: a magnifier slides over the hull wall
a hairline crack draws across the surface
the wall's layers show in section
two layers peel apart, red gap

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 2019, a worker spotted a hairline crack. It started at a delamination, where layers inside the carbon had come apart.

params.place: the engineering office, evening

moments.what: an engineer's desk lamp clicks on over a sign-off form
a stamp hovers: HULL DONE
the signature line stays empty
the trip's form slides away
the lamp switches off, the chair empty

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The director of engineering said that hull was done, and would not sign off on the next trip. He was let go soon after.

params.place: Titan with its fairing cut away, in a studio of dark water

moments.what: a new black cylinder turns in the light, fairing cut away
a caption types on: five bonded layers
the camera pushes in on the carbon wall
the thickness tag counts up

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So a second hull was built: five bonded layers of carbon fibre, about 5 inches thick in all.

params.place: the deep ocean test facility

moments.what: the full hull lowers into a big test chamber
the chamber's gauge climbs
the gauge stops at its figure
a tag stamps: in service

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: How was the new hull proven? It was pressure tested once, in 2021, to a simulated 4,200 metres. Then it went to work.

params.place: a pressure test tank in a laboratory

moments.what: a second scale model lowers into the tank
a wrinkle ripples in its wall
the model crumples, red
a dashed line marks the wreck's depth below it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its own test models failed too. One, wrinkled inside, imploded at 2,800 metres, shallower than the Titanic.

params.place: in front of Titan's window, deep water

moments.what: the camera swings round to the front dome, its window glowing
a certificate tag pins to the window
the rating plate counts up
the camera pulls back; far below, the wreck's depth plate lights red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And the window in the front dome? Its maker certified it to just 1,000 metres. The wreck lies at 3,880.

params.place: Titan with its fairing cut away, in a studio of dark water

moments.what: the front dome lights amber
the rings light
the window glows
a tag pins on: from the first hull
the parts settle back in place

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its domes, its rings and its window were not new. They came off the first hull, and were used again.

moments.what: signatures fill the bottom of a letter
the letterhead types on
a line highlights

the last word underlines

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 2018, dozens of submarine experts signed a draft letter of concern. It warned the experimental approach could end in catastrophe.

a ship stamp appears in the corner

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Was Titan ever certified by a classification society, the bodies that check ships? No. OceanGate dropped the idea.

a sound ring bursts off the hull, the frame shakes

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So Titan went to sea without it. And one day, on the way up from the Titanic, everyone heard a bang.

moments.what: the chapter card types on: the warnings

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 2021 and 2022, Titan reached the wreck 13 times.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On one dive in 2022, its batteries died before it could land back on its platform. The guests spent the night inside, on the surface.

Titan rises toward the light

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On dive 80, in July 2022, as Titan climbed back up, the guests inside and a boat crew on the surface heard a loud bang.

moments.what: a question mark pulses over the dive card
a small group of figures at the rail
a speech note writes: shifted

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What was it? The guests were told the hull had shifted in its cradle.

the spike holds

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Titan carried sensors that listened for cracking in the hull. On dive 80, they showed a burst of noise, and a sudden jump in strain.

params.place: the expedition's dive log on the chart table

moments.what: the reported words type on as text
the chart dims

each new card gets a red edge

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The chief looked at the data, and wanted to keep diving. Titan went down three more times that summer.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Investigators later found the hull was likely damaged after dive 80, with layers coming apart inside the wall.

parked cars and bay lines around it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: After that summer, Titan was left outside in a parking lot in St. John's, uncovered, as winter came.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 2023, it no longer rode on a ship's deck. It was towed behind the ship, on its platform, through the open sea.

beats.say: On one trip, in high seas, it lost part of its outer shell. Divers had to make repairs.

moments.what: a snowflake tag drops on the log

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Cold, towing, time. OceanGate never tested what they did to the hull. Dive 88 would show it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: June 18. The support ship Polar Prince reaches the dive site early in the morning.

moments.what: five small figures cross to the open dome
the last one steps in
the deck crew stand still at the rail
the sound drops, only the swell

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Five people climb inside. Then everyone, on the sub and the ship, takes a few silent minutes to check the plan.

moments.what: two divers swim along the platform

Titan lifts off and drops away

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Divers sink the platform. Titan lets go, and starts down. It is the first dive this year deeper than 10 metres.

moments.what: a dive profile draws on the ocean cut
the line slopes down to the seabed

it climbs back to the surface

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The plan: two and a half hours down, three hours at the wreck, and two and a half hours back up.

moments.what: the operations room lights
the depth bar slides down
the readout climbs
the clock ticks on
a message pair types on: check, OK

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: How does the ship keep track? A screen shows its depth, and every ten to fifteen minutes, ship and sub trade text messages.

moments.what: Titan sinks past the camera
the last light dies above

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Down it goes, past where any sunlight reaches, into total darkness, with only its own lamps for light.

params.place: the operations room on the Polar Prince

moments.what: the depth readout reaches the figure
the message types on
two weights drop on the side panel
the status light glows green

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At 3,363 metres, Titan sends a message: it has dropped two weights, a normal step to slow down near the bottom.

params.place: the operations room on the Polar Prince

moments.what: the clock ticks a minute
the reply sends
the line stays empty
two more messages stack up
the tracking dot goes grey: lost

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: A minute later, the ship replies. No answer. They send again, and again. Silence.

params.place: beside Titan in the deep dark

moments.what: the camera circles Titan in the dark
the hull begins to glow amber
a depth tag types on beside it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What happened in those seconds, more than three kilometres down?

moments.what: the hull wall section draws, its gaps red

the patch folds in

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The weakened wall gave way in one spot. Investigators call it a local buckling failure.

params.place: beside Titan in the deep dark

moments.what: the hull's colour climbs to red, in silence
a last ping ring leaves the sub
a crack runs around the cylinder
a white flash, the hull crushes inward, bubbles burst out

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: 7 seconds after its last message, the hull imploded.

params.place: the deep water far from the wreck, in silence

moments.what: far away, a cloud of bubbles rises in the dark; an age tag types on
five small figures dim on the memorial strip
the camera eases closer
the camera rises slowly toward the faint surface

things: five small figures for the people aboard

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The youngest aboard, Suleman Dawood, was 19. He had come along with his father.

params.place: the operations room on the Polar Prince

moments.what: the operations room, the operator at the console
a tag pins on: comms fault?
the signal bars flicker empty
messages stack up unanswered
the clock spins forward

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Up on the ship, they believed the acoustic link had dropped, and kept sending messages for hours.

params.place: the operations room on the Polar Prince

moments.what: the plan's page slides onto the console
a line highlights: ascend
the clock's hand sweeps an hour
the surface marker stays empty
the operator stands at the window

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: OceanGate's own plan said Titan must head back up an hour after losing contact. It never came up.

params.place: the search area on the surface, overcast

moments.what: a search plane crosses the grey sky
an oxygen clock counts down on the tag
the clock holds
ships' lights dot the horizon
the camera sinks below the surface into black

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The world watched a countdown of 96 hours of oxygen. Ships and planes searched the surface, but Titan was already gone.

params.place: the search area on the surface, overcast

moments.what: a grey cargo plane crosses the overcast sky
its shadow sweeps the sea
a tag types on: robots rated for the wreck
the plane banks toward the ships

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Only a few robots in the world could reach that depth. One was flown in by a military cargo plane.

params.place: the seabed near the Titanic's bow

moments.what: an underwater robot's lamps sweep the seabed
the robot drifts into view
the tail cone lights in its beam
two domes light up
a distance line draws to the wreck's bow

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: After a 4 day search, a robot found the tail cone and both domes on the seabed, about 500 metres from the Titanic's bow.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the chapter card types on: the findings
the report's cover slides onto the desk
the page turns
a stamp lands: preventable

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Two investigations followed. The U.S. Coast Guard's board called the loss of five lives preventable.

moments.what: the safety board's report page settles
the camera pushes in on the probable cause
the line highlights
the line underlines

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The National Transportation Safety Board named the probable cause: OceanGate's inadequate engineering process.

params.place: Titan with its fairing cut away, in a studio of dark water

moments.what: the camera circles the bare carbon cylinder
the finding types on and stamps: cause
the cylinder's stress colour pulses
the camera eases back

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It never established how strong and durable the hull really was.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the findings page settles
the camera slides down to the sixth finding
the line highlights
the dive number underlines

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its reading of the sensor data was flawed, so it never saw that Titan was damaged after dive 80.

params.place: a harbour-side parking lot in St. John's, winter

moments.what: back in the snowy lot, the finding card pins on
snow settles on Titan
the finding's line types on
it stamps: cause

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It never understood what being stored outdoors, and towed through rough seas, could do to the hull.

params.place: the investigation board

moments.what: the third finding pins on
a rule book outline lights
it stamps: factor
the board lights all three

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And the rules for passenger submersibles were too weak to make it follow industry standards.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the Coast Guard report's page settles
a phrase highlights
it underlines
a second phrase highlights
the camera pulls back over the page

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The Coast Guard's board also pointed to a toxic workplace culture, and said OceanGate used intimidation to dodge scrutiny.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the findings page settles
finding seven highlights
it underlines
the camera eases back
the page dims

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: With a proper emergency plan, the safety board said, rescue help would likely have been standing by. A rescue was not possible this time.

params.place: the seabed near the Titanic's bow

moments.what: the robot's lamps light the debris
a red ring outlines the broken hull
the camera rises off the seabed

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Two boards, the same answer. So what has changed since?

moments.what: the chapter card types on: what changed
the recommendations page settles
the heading highlights
the first recommendation highlights
it underlines

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The safety board made 4 recommendations to the Coast Guard. First, study how passenger submersibles are run today.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the camera slides to the second recommendation
it highlights
it underlines
a small figure stamp lands in the margin

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then write U.S. rules for pressure vessels that carry people.

moments.what: ships from many countries ride the swell under a clear sky
a caption types on: the world standard for submersibles
a stamp lands: mandatory
the camera drifts on along the line of ships

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And push for the world's standard for these vessels to become mandatory, not optional.

params.place: the expedition's dive log on the chart table

moments.what: a stack of recommendation cards builds on the log
the count tag settles
each card gets a pending tag
a gavel outline waits, unstruck

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The Coast Guard's own board added 17 recommendations. Today, those are proposals. Whether they become law is still to come.

params.place: the expedition's dive log on the chart table

moments.what: the dive card with the bang flashes
the cards between slide past one by one
each one gets a dive stamp
the last card turns red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The bang came on dive 80. Titan kept diving. The hull failed on dive 88.

params.place: the investigation board

moments.what: link one stamps
link two stamps
link three stamps

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: An uncertified hull. A window rated far short of the depth. A bang explained away. A hull left out in the cold.
